name: OpenWork v0.18.58
body:
## Run OpenWork Web on your own self-hosted deployment

- **Self-host OpenWork Web and team tools on AWS.** For self-hosters: run OpenWork Web with sandboxed browser workspaces, and deploy Slack, Workbot, and Automations that run without a desktop. AWS deployments can use existing networks and load balancers, and can connect to an existing cluster or runner fleet.
- **Connect OpenCode 2 to your organization.** If you use OpenWork from OpenCode: the `opencode-openwork` plugin brings in your organization's AI Gateway models, tools, and skills after sign-in, without the desktop app. You can also upgrade desktop chats to OpenCode 2 with a backup first; its conversations can use the built-in browser and discover connected tools reliably.
- **Admins get clearer controls and reporting.** Organization Analytics is back, with restored usage and workflow history where available. When enabled, admins can also report on skills, plugins, and connectors, set member, admin, and team permissions, and choose a default model for cloud agents; Audit Logs now cover more organization activity.
- **Chat and daily work recover more smoothly.** Pasted text and images stay at the cursor, reopened Apps load their data, migrated chats with a missing agent can answer again, and OpenWork keeps the Working status visible during quiet stretches. Ollama keeps multiple selected models and their thinking choices; Drive uploads respect your chosen Google account.
- **Calendar, Workbot, and connections do more.** When Calendar features are enabled, add or edit Automations alongside meetings; Workbot can recover stopped tasks. When enabled, admins can check when connections were last verified, and compatible MCP clients can subscribe to remote-session updates.
- **Some familiar pages and searches have changed.** Organization dashboards and admin-assigned dashboards in Desktop are gone, while personal dashboards remain. “Search sessions” now searches session titles and workspace names, not message text; for organizations with OpenWork Models, Auto is replaced in the model picker by GPT-6 Luna.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · [Compare](https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/compare/v0.18.57...v0.18.58)

name: v5.1.32
body:
**5.1.32 is the release that 5.1.31 was meant to be: 5.1.31 never reached npm.** Two checks in the release pipeline stopped it before any package was published, one on the macOS Intel desktop engine and one on the Linux musl builds. omo itself did not change between the two, so every entry below is new to anyone upgrading from 5.1.30. The notarization check now waits for Apple's ticket to reach Gatekeeper, and the musl smoke no longer reports an exited host supervisor as a leak. ([#10081](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10081), [#10082](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10082))

**omo runs on senpi 2026.10.12, and long sessions stop growing with every shell command.** A finished bash session used to keep its whole headless terminal screen (10,000 lines of scrollback plus replay history, about 20 MB for a 4,000-line output) until the 32-session limit evicted it, so a busy session or task host grew by that much per command; it now keeps only its final visible screen and its bounded output, and a live terminal's replay history is stored as flat strings instead of about 31 bytes per character. After an accepted compaction, prompts, retries and resumes use the compacted context, so a session that fits is no longer refused with "Context remains above the compaction threshold" or compacted twice. When one provider account runs out of quota, its other models are skipped, compaction runs on a model that can still answer, and the error names the provider, the reset time and the `/model` way out instead of raw 429 JSON. ChatGPT-subscription GPT-6.1 Sol, Fast and Ultrafast get a 500,000-token context window. Web search uses the active model's own server-side search first on routes where it was tested live, and falls back once to the standalone search if that fails. Prompt-cache prewarm is now opt-in (`promptCache.keepAlive.enabled`) and starts only on your first edit, never on session start or resume. RPC clients gain `eval_cells.list`/`peek`/`stop`, and a shared host that is shutting down refuses new sessions with `host_stopping` instead of adopting them. Thanks to @MoerAI and @Bearmancer. ([senpi#3171](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3171), [senpi#3170](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3170), [senpi#3137](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3137), [senpi#3062](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3062), [senpi#3131](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3131), [senpi#3150](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3150), [senpi#3122](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3122), [senpi#3140](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3140), [senpi#3072](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3072), [senpi#3059](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3059), [senpi#3101](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/issues/3101), [senpi#3055](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/senpi/pull/3055)) ([#10069](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10069))

**The Recommended model profile is gone: with no model profile set, OmO starts on Daily · Normal.** A fresh OmO Desktop or headless session with no `model_profile` applies Daily · Normal (Claude Opus 5.5, then Kimi K3, then GLM 5.3). If none of those is connected, it uses the first lane that is: Daily · Heavy, Geeky · Normal, then Geeky · Heavy, so a ChatGPT-only setup starts on Geeky · Normal. A config that still says `model_profile: "recommended"` gets the same default and one log line; it is never an error, and `omo.json` is not rewritten. A `model_profiles.recommended` you defined yourself still applies. The interactive TUI is unchanged. Requested by @code-yeongyu. ([#10029](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/10029))

**Session tools find sessions kept in OpenCode's older storage, and show the real error instead of `[object Object]`.** A session that exists only in OpenCode's legacy JSON storage is listed, but the SQLite server answers `NotFoundError` for it; `session_search`, `session_list`, `session_read` and `session_info` now read such a session from the older storage instead of failing. Any other error reads as its name and message, and when `session_search` or `session_list` (without a date filter) still cannot read a session, it skips it and names it at the end instead of failing the whole call. Thanks to @crazyrabbit0 for the reproduction. ([#5854](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/5854), [#10041](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10041))

**Ultrawork tracks task-owned worktrees and runtime caches when they are created.** Cleanup guidance now scopes cache paths before task commands, requires path-specific todos and removal receipts, and preserves worktrees still needed by open PRs without wiping shared caches. Native full and compact directives, Codex, and OpenCode variants carry the same lifecycle; co-loaded workflows refer to it instead of repeating it. ([#9951](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9951), [#9953](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9953))
**Computer use can list and choose menu commands on Linux.** On X11 and Wayland, `menus.items` and `menus.select` walk a window's menu bar through AT-SPI and run the chosen item's own activation action, without focusing or raising the window. The request is bound to the exact window you named, so a same-titled sibling window of the same app is refused rather than used, and ambiguous, disabled or submenu labels are refused before anything runs. Selecting a menu command also no longer crashes GTK apps on Ubuntu 22.04. ([#9651](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9651), [#9994](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9994))

**Computer use can take a screenshot and read a window's accessibility tree in one step.** `observe()` on a window returns both together, and a failed or cancelled observation normally leaves the previous screenshot and accessibility references in place. ([#9651](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9651))

**Computer use can zoom into part of a screenshot at full detail without changing where clicks land.** `zoom(region)` on the desktop, a window or a display captures that region again at native resolution, while later clicks and typing still use the coordinates of the last full screenshot. ([#9651](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9651))

**Computer use can list and choose menu commands on Windows.** `menus.items` and `menus.select` read a window's classic menu bar directly, or its UI Automation menu when it has none, and run the chosen command without keyboard input. Elevated windows, ambiguous or disabled labels, submenus, and menus that change mid-request are refused before anything runs; apps that take focus while they act are refused in the background and work with `delivery: "foreground"`. ([#9651](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9651), [#9991](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9991))

**Computer use screenshots the monitor you are working on by default, and `computer.display(id)` reaches any other one.** An unset `computer.display` now captures the active monitor, the one the focused window mostly sits on, instead of compositing every display; `"all"` and display ids work as before. `computer.display("all" | "active" | id)` gives a screenshot and input handle for one display without changing the session default, and `computer.displays()` lists every monitor. ([#9651](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9651), [#9995](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9995))

**OpenCode requests now follow the selected model's live capabilities instead of a stale model cache.** When OpenCode passes the live model to `chat.params`, its variants, thinking support, temperature support and output limit take precedence over the cached provider list, and the SDK's `provider.info.id` provider context is accepted alongside `provider.id`; calls that carry only model IDs keep the cached and bundled fallback. Thanks to @MoerAI. ([#10001](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/10001))

**`background_task.taskCleanupDelayMs` now also sets how long finished background tasks stay retrievable.** A delay longer than 30 minutes is no longer cut short; leaving it unset keeps the existing timing. Thanks to @imadal1n. ([#9984](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9984))

**The MCP OAuth callback server answers errors in plain text.** Its not-found, provider-error and missing-parameter responses are now sent as `text/plain; charset=utf-8` with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so an `error_description` in the callback URL is shown as text and never rendered as HTML. MCP sign-in currently runs through a second callback server that never echoed that text, so nothing you see changes; consolidating the two is tracked separately. Thanks to @niStee. ([#6464](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/6464), [#9979](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9979))

**OpenCode task delegation and team creation now honor `claude_code.agents: false`, so disabled Claude Code agents fail fast instead of being selected.** Thanks to @cynkai. ([#8744](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/8744), [#8802](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/8802))

**Delegated OpenCode sessions show their task category in the title.** Background, synchronous and fallback-created child sessions prefix the category while keeping the description and agent suffix; tasks without a category keep their existing title. ([#6854](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/6854), [#7256](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/7256))

**OpenCode runtime fallback can switch models after a provider content-filter error.** When fallback is enabled and alternate models are configured, a blocked response advances to a different model; the existing attempt limit and chain exhaustion still stop retries. ([#6796](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/6796), [#7257](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/7257))

**Memory facts are extracted only after you type a prompt.** Pending facts no longer start a model call when a session starts, rebinds, resumes or forks; extraction waits for a real prompt of yours in a top-level session. It runs on `memory.facts.model`, a configured quick chain or the session's own model, and with none of those available the queue stays pending without recording a failure. ([#9922](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9922), [#9954](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9954))

**Naming a `ulw-*` skill no longer switches on ultrawork.** `ulw-plan`, `ulw-research`, `ulw-execute` and `ulw-loop` in a prompt leave ultrawork off, while a bare `ulw` or `ultrawork` still turns it on. ([#6876](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/6876), [#7255](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/7255))

**Tests now catch environment leaks at the file that causes them.** A test file that leaves `process.env` changed fails with the names of the changed keys, and the next file starts from a clean environment. Thanks to @Dante-dan. ([#9390](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/issues/9390), [#9469](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/9469))

name: CC Switch v4.0.10
body:
# CC Switch v4.0.10

### 4.0 正式版的第六个修复版本

这一版的重点是一键导入链接（`ccswitch://` 深度链接）：CC Switch 没在运行时点链接不会再丢；链接可以声明接口格式、导入 Pi 供应商、带上网站自己的图标；Codex 和 Grok Build 的链接保留供应商自带的配置，不再被换成固定模板；确认框里可以选导入后是否立即切换。同时发布了中、英、日三语的站长接入指南和在线链接生成器。供应商图标现在可以上传本地图片，存进「我的图标」后所有供应商都能选用；用量页新增首字时间，没开路由也能按会话日志估算。另外修复了路由模式下 Claude Code 的 haiku 档请求被要求思考的上游拒绝、v3.20 及更早用官方账号走路由留下的 Codex 会话打不开、Grok Build 第三方供应商生成不了会话标题等问题。4.0 完整的更新内容请见 [v4.0 发布说明](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.4-zh.md)。

**[English →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.10-en.md) | [日本語版 →](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/release-notes/v4.0.10-ja.md)**

---

## 一键导入链接

### 用户能感受到的变化

- **CC Switch 没在运行时点链接，不会再丢。** 以前在 Windows 和 Linux 上，CC Switch 没开着时点一键导入链接，应用会启动，但导入确认框不出现；轻量模式下窗口重建时也会丢。macOS 上同一个链接会弹两次确认框。现在链接会先存下来，确认框显示出来之后才算处理完，中途被打断也不会丢，后到的旧链接也不会盖掉新链接。
- **确认框里可以选导入后是否立即切换。** 供应商链接的确认框新增「导入后立即切换到这个供应商」开关，默认关闭，打开时会提示客户端请求将改发到链接里的地址。OpenCode、OpenClaw、Hermes、MiniMax Code 这类共存式应用是「导入后立即添加到 OpenCode 配置」这样的开关，Pi 是「导入后立即在 Pi 中启用」，这两类默认打开；提示词是「导入后立即启用」。链接里的 `enabled` 只决定开关的初始状态。关掉开关就只保存供应商，不改客户端配置，即使这是该应用的第一个供应商。
- **带用量查询脚本的链接，导入后默认开启用量查询。** 站长在链接里附上脚本，就是想让你导入后直接看到余额，以前还要再手动打开一次。链接写了 `usageEnabled=false` 时仍然关闭；不带脚本的链接和以前一样。脚本在沙箱里运行，只能向供应商地址的同源 HTTPS 发一次请求，确认框里照常完整显示脚本内容。
- **Codex 链接保留供应商自带的配置。** 链接带完整 `config.toml` 时，以前只取出 Key、地址和模型，再套进固定模板，供应商的认证方式、请求头、WebSocket 支持和模型目录地址都会丢。现在保留其中属于这个供应商的部分：连接和认证字段、模型、推理强度、上下文窗口、子代理模型等；模型目录地址只在和接口地址同源时保留，因为 Codex 拉取它时会带上供应商的凭据。`[features]`、MCP、权限这类全局设置不导入。会让 Codex 执行命令或读取本机凭据的供应商配置（`auth`、`aws`、`gateway_oauth`、`env_http_headers`）整条拒绝。不带配置的链接导入结果和以前逐字一致。
- **Grok Build 链接保留模型配置。** 带 `config.toml` 的链接以前也会被换成固定模板，丢掉显示名、说明、接口类型和上下文窗口。现在保留 `[models] default` 指向的那张模型表，地址、Key 和模型仍以链接参数为准；用到 `auth_provider`、`env_http_headers`、`mtls_cert_dir` 的链接会被拒绝。一个供应商在 Grok Build 里只占一张表，所以其他模型表不导入。
- **会被展开执行的值一律拒绝。** 共存式应用会展开配置里的一些特殊写法：Pi 里以 `!` 开头的值会被当成命令执行，`$NAME` / `${NAME}` 会读环境变量；OpenCode 有 `{env:}` / `{file:}`；OpenClaw 和 Hermes 有 `${...}`。链接里出现这些写法时，可能执行命令，或者把本机的密钥和文件内容发到链接里的地址。现在解析链接、合并配置和生成供应商时都会检查，发现就拒绝导入。
- **其他：** 带 `configUrl` 的链接现在一打开就提示不支持，不会等你确认后才失败；提示词链接支持 MiniMax Code，MCP 链接支持 Pi 和 MiniMax Code；导入供应商后托盘菜单会立即刷新。

### 站长能用的新参数

- **`apiFormat`：** 一个参数声明上游的接口格式（`anthropic` / `openai_chat` / `openai_responses` / `gemini_native`），CC Switch 会换成各应用自己的字段。Claude Code、Codex、Grok Build 的非原生格式需要开启本地路由；应用不支持的组合在解析时就会被拒绝。不带这个参数的链接行为不变。
- **Pi 供应商链接：** 新增支持，导入后写进 Pi 的 `models.json`，链接必须带模型。
- **`iconUrl`：** 填网站自己 logo 的 https 地址。确认框打开时就下载并显示在顶部，导入后作为卡片的自定义图标；下载失败不影响导入，卡片退回内置图标或名称首字母。图片会重绘成小尺寸 PNG 保存，地址本身不保存也不渲染。下载时只连公网地址，并锁定解析结果，防止第二次 DNS 解析指向别处；重定向逐跳检查，最多 3 跳。不走系统代理、不带 Cookie，5 秒超时，最大 256 KB，文件类型必须和内容一致。

### 站长接入指南和在线生成器

- **[站长接入指南](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/guides/deeplink-site-integration-guide-zh.md)**（另有 [English](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/guides/deeplink-site-integration-guide-en.md)、[日本語](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/docs/guides/deeplink-site-integration-guide-ja.md)）：怎么生成链接、怎么在页面上放「一键导入」按钮（点按钮时再向后端取链接，Key 不会出现在页面源码里）、用户没装 CC Switch 时显示什么、怎么附上用量查询脚本。用 New API 或 Sub2API 搭的站，Key 列表里已经自带「导入到 CC Switch」按钮；区别是 New API 的链接不带用量查询脚本，用户导入后看不到余额。
- **[在线链接生成器](https://ccswitch.io/deplink.html)**：从测试页改成给站长用的生成器，分供应商、MCP、提示词、Skill 四类，按应用列出可选的 `apiFormat`，内置用量脚本模板，填 `icon` / `iconUrl` 时按应用内同样的规则检查。用户手册里原来的生成器链接指向一个从没开通的 GitHub Pages 地址，打开是 404，现在手册和 README 都改指这里。

## 新增

**供应商图标可以上传本地图片，存进「我的图标」反复使用。** 图标选择器分成「我的图标」和「内置图标」两组，搜索框同时筛两组。点「我的图标」第一格的「上传」，选一张 PNG、JPG、WebP 或 SVG（不超过 2 MB），起个名字（默认是文件名）就存进「我的图标」并用在当前供应商上；以后其他供应商、其他应用都能直接选，不用再传一次，重复上传同一张图会复用已有的那条。鼠标移到图标上可以重命名或删除；卡片保存的是图片本身，所以重命名、删除都不影响已经在用它的供应商。图片会缩成 96×96 的 PNG，「我的图标」和供应商配置都随云同步带走，不在磁盘上另存文件；SVG 会先转成位图，里面的脚本和外部请求都不会执行，原始文件不进数据库。一键导入链接带来的网站图标会以「当前图标」显示，可以存进「我的图标」。选择器现在点一下图标就选好并关闭，去掉图标点搜索框旁的「清除图标」。

**用量页显示首字时间。** 路由服务一直记录首字时间，以前只在悬停提示和请求详情里能看到。现在供应商统计和模型统计新增「首字」列，取经路由服务的成功流式请求的中位数，偶尔排队、冷启动的慢请求不会把它拉高；请求日志在「速度」后面也加了「首字」列。没开路由时，按会话日志的时间戳估算，带 ≈ 显示：Claude Code 看以思考开头的回复，Codex 看较新版本写入的时间戳；以正文或工具调用开头的回复没有估算值。升级前导入的记录不补算。

**用量查询新增 Sub2API 模板。** 「配置用量查询」的模板里新增 Sub2API，只需要供应商的 Key 和地址，地址带不带 `/v1` 都行；会显示套餐名，额度不限的订阅不再显示成负余额。

**新增预设：** NekoCode（Claude Code、Claude Desktop、Codex、OpenCode、OpenClaw、Hermes、Pi，MiniMax Code 沿用 Pi 预设）。YYLX 在中文界面显示为「鱼鱼连线」（繁体中文为「魚魚連線」）。

## 修复

- **路由模式下 Claude Code 的 haiku 档请求被上游拒绝**（[#8118](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8118)）。路由模式往 `settings.json` 里写的是固定的模型别名，Claude Code 按别名决定怎么发思考参数。haiku 档以前写的是 `claude-haiku-4-5`，Claude Code 认为这个模型可以关思考，就发出关闭思考的请求，要求必须开思考的上游会直接拒绝。现在改成 `claude-haiku-5-5`，和 sonnet、opus 档的发法一致。路由本身仍按「haiku」关键词映射，选到哪个模型不变。
- **v3.20 及更早用官方账号走路由留下的 Codex 会话打不开**（[#7948](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7948)）。v3.17 到 v3.20 用官方账号走本地路由时，Codex 把会话记在 `cc-switch-official` 名下；v4.0 不再写这张表，Codex 恢复这些会话时就会报「Model provider `cc-switch-official` not found」。现在 CC Switch 启动时会把它们移回 Codex 内置的 `openai` 分组，只改会话记录，不碰 `config.toml`。这些会话本来就用官方登录，Codex 也一直把它们当 OpenAI 处理，移动后行为不变。
- **Grok Build 用第三方供应商时生成不了会话标题**（[#7003](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7003)）。没设 `models.session_summary` 时，Grok Build 用内置的 `grok-4.6` 生成标题，却把请求发到默认模型表的地址，第三方上游会拒绝。现在切换供应商时，`session_summary` 在没设或指向 CC Switch 写的表时会跟着指向当前供应商，切回官方账号时删掉；你自己设的内置模型或自己的表保持不动。
- **OpenRouter、Novita 余额为零时卡片显示「套餐已过期」**（[#8148](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/8148)）。余额为零或为负时，Key 其实还能用，卡片和托盘却显示套餐已过期。现在显示「余额已用完」；接口返回缺失或格式不对的余额时报错，不再当成零余额。
- **Codex 中途换模型后，用量记在了原来的模型上。** Codex 在线程设置里换模型时，日志里不一定会写新的轮次上下文，用量导入以前会把之后的请求记在上一个模型名下（没有更早记录时记成 `unknown`），价格也按原模型算。现在会读取这条设置。已经导入的记录不会自动改写，源会话日志还在的话，可以在用量页的「数据来源」里点「重建 Codex 用量」（重建前会自动备份数据库）。
- **在设置里改了配置目录、还没点保存，改另一项设置时目录也被保存了**（[#7849](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/issues/7849)）。其他设置自动保存时，现在只会带上已确认的目录；被放弃的草稿也不会再留在输入框里。
- **Windows 上打开添加或编辑供应商页面时窗口闪一下。** v4.0.9 修了编辑页先显示加载页的问题，但整页的淡入淡出在 Windows 上仍会闪。现在这两个页面不再做淡入淡出，其他页面不受影响。
- **Windows 上删掉的桌面快捷方式，每次更新都会被装回来。** MSI 升级会先卸载旧版再完整安装新版，以前每次都会重新创建桌面快捷方式。现在只在全新安装时创建；升级时只有原来的快捷方式还在才保留。

**其他：** 「连接模式」的说明改为先讲每种模式的长处：直连最原生，路由可热切换供应商、支持故障转移和格式转换，聚合可在客户端内无缝切换多家模型。用量页的所有表格列统一左对齐，请求日志里供应商和模型两列让出一些宽度给数字列。日文界面把「高級オプション」改为「詳細オプション」。

## 升级说明

**数据库结构没有变化**，仍然是 20。

- 已经在用路由模式的 Claude Code，升级后启动 CC Switch 时会把新的 haiku 别名写进 `settings.json`，新开的 Claude Code 会话会用上。
- Codex 会话的迁移在 CC Switch 启动时自动进行，每个 Codex 配置目录只做一次，改动前的会话记录备份在原有的会话分组迁移备份目录。如果你手动恢复过 `cc-switch-official` 表并且仍在使用，这次迁移会跳过。
- 新增预设只影响新添加的供应商。

---

## 致谢

感谢 @funkpopo（OpenRouter 余额为零时显示套餐已过期、Codex 中途换模型后用量记错模型）、@hulkbig（设置自动保存时带上未确认的目录）、@NestorRay（Windows 上打开供应商页面时的闪烁）的贡献。

感谢 @hao-lin-lwh、@desmonna、@mossonli、@enderzcx、@nbcoming、@liyangdeamo-svg、@linhay、@aofee 报告问题、提供复现信息和帮忙验证。

完整的技术细节请见 [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。

name: v2.11.27 — Analysis rules from the Magister benchmark (#573). Four rules, each written into the ski…
body:
- **Analysis rules from the Magister benchmark** (#573). Four rules, each written into the skill and mirrored in its description so hosted agents see them before opening the file:
  - **ad-creative** (2.10.0 → 2.11.0): a new Test Hypotheses That Can Lose section. A hypothesis names the metric, the comparison, and the expected direction.
  - **copywriting** (2.1.0 → 2.2.0): claims must be supportable, and a declined claim names the evidence that would unlock it.
  - **analytics** (2.0.3 → 2.1.0): compute metrics from row-level data, and divide rates only over matching closed windows.
  - **marketing-plan** (1.2.1 → 1.2.2): AARRR stage metrics count only cohorts whose window has closed.

  ad-creative also notes that Magister can run its data-pull step (#567), with a disclosure that Magister is the maintainer's product and alternatives for running the pull yourself.
- **influencer-marketing** (1.1.2 → 1.2.0) and **social** (2.3.3 → 2.3.4): Telegram channel ads (#785 by @Courier-Britva). The new `references/telegram-channels.md` covers how placements are bought, a seven-check vetting routine based on views per subscriber, and pricing by CPM and deletion window. Contributed by the team behind TGScope, which is disclosed; its benchmarks come from TGScope's own studies and are labeled as directional.
- **Tools:**
  - **rowbound** guide (#500, closes #498): an open-source, self-hosted alternative to Clay that runs enrichment waterfalls from a Google Sheet, with a CLI and MCP.
  - **AIsa** joins as a ◆ Skill Partner in SEO tools (#783).
  - Across the CLIs, rejected HTTP requests now exit 1 (#713), and invalid flags fail with structured errors before any request is sent (#732), both by @rudycelekli.

## Skill ZIP assets

Complete source catalog: 50 skills.
Claude web target: 50 skills with reviewed short descriptions.

Choose `<name>-claude-web.zip` for the documented single-folder web upload format.
Source ZIPs retain original metadata; they are not substitutes for omitted web ZIPs.
Live client upload, account limits, and invocation behavior have not been verified.

Web omissions (also recorded in `claude-web-manifest.json`):
- None.

name: SDK v0.0.93
body:
- Plugins load in-process through one registry per process instead of a node/bun subprocess, so the compiled CLI and its hub no longer need a runtime on PATH, and plugins can use the Bun global under the Bun-built hub. `CLINE_PLUGIN_MODE=sandbox` keeps the subprocess sandbox. The registry wraps import, setup, hooks, tools and commands with timeouts and error capture, and tracks each plugin's state (loading/ready/degraded/failed/disabled) with its last error. A failing plugin no longer silently drops its tools: `session.create` accepts a `plugins` policy and returns `pluginIssues`, later failures reach affected sessions as status notices, the hub answers `plugins.list`/`plugins.status`/`plugins.reload` and broadcasts `plugin.status_changed`, and the daemon marks a plugin failed instead of shutting down when an uncaught error comes from it. Each session gets its own copy of every plugin module, so plugins that keep per-session state at module level keep working
- Turning reasoning off now works on every provider, not just a fixed list. Models whose catalog entry has no off option are sent nothing and keep their default, and models without a `reasoning` capability are skipped. Gemini and Vertex send exact `thinkingBudget` values only to models that advertise a budget; level-only Gemini models get a thinking level instead (they rejected `thinkingBudget`). A request never carries both the portable reasoning option and a native provider control (`effort`, `thinking`, `thinkingConfig`, …); the native one wins
- The `cline` provider's default model is the first entry of the Cline recommended-models list, falling back to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5`. `CLINE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` moves from Claude Sonnet 5 to Claude Sonnet 5.5, and the `openrouter` provider default is now `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5` too
- `estimateRequestInputTokens` and `createTokenEstimator` no longer bill base64 image payloads at the text rate. A ~90 KB screenshot counted as ~30k tokens, so a few images triggered auto compaction long before the transcript was near budget. Each image now adds a flat `ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_IMAGE` (1600). New `createImageAwareReplacer` export in `@cline/shared`
- Auto compaction uses the resolved model's context window. When the discovered catalog entry had no limit but the selected-model override did, compaction was handed the bare catalog entry and ran against the wrong budget
- Scheduled runs: queued runs are claimed correctly under `bun:sqlite`, which bound the store's named parameters as NULL so the desktop hub never claimed a queued run and it stayed pending with no error. Runs whose agent turn ends with a provider error (such as a retired model id) are now recorded as failed with the error message instead of succeeding silently, and the run report keeps usage and tool calls. Queued cron occurrences superseded by a newer occurrence of the same schedule are cancelled, so a backlog no longer replays every missed slot back to back
- Rule files that are symlinks are now loaded from config directories instead of skipped. Edits to a link's target are picked up on the next refresh or new session
- `resolveSkillsConfigSearchPaths` scans `.claude/skills`, so skills authored for Claude Code are visible to Cline
- The editor tool advertises `old_text` as a plain string. When the schema allowed null, some models sent null instead of the replacement text. Null is still accepted at runtime and treated as omitted
- Composio connectors: signed-in sessions register Composio's meta tools (search, manage connections, wait for connections, multi-execute), so the agent can find connector tools across toolkits, hand the user a Connect Link for an app that is not connected yet, and run what it found. Connector tools are discovered through meta search; saved desktop connection state no longer supplies model tools. Hosts can supply their own authentication through the new `connectorsRequest` option (`ConnectorsRequest` exported from `@cline/core`), which is also forwarded to scheduled sessions. `resolveComposioToolsStatePath` is renamed to `resolveComposioConnectionStatePath`
- The Cline cloud sign-in helpers in `@cline/core` accept an `AbortSignal`, so hosts can cancel a pending sign-in while it is polling
- Cloud session refreshes update open sessions with titles renamed on the web, and keep renames made locally while a refresh is in flight
- Refreshed the model catalog (6,572 → 6,862 models). Adds the AI/ML API, LowRouter, and Prime Inference providers. models.dev no longer lists v0, so the `v0` provider ships with only its default model, `v0-1.5-md`. OpenCode Go's base URL moves from `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` to `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1`. The Cline free list adds Step 5 Preview. Default models change for 302.AI, CrossModel, Cortecs, DigitalOcean, NEAR AI Cloud, and Ofox (Claude Haiku 5.5), DevPass (LLM Gateway), LLM Gateway, and Meta (Muse Wonder 1.0), Aixy (GPT-6.1 Sol), CloudFerro Sherlock and Moark (GLM 5.3), Ambient, NanoGPT, Neuralwatt, and Novita AI

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/sdk/sdk/v0.0.92...sdk/sdk/v0.0.93

name: CLI v3.0.71
body:
- Plugins now load inside the hub instead of a separate node or bun process, so the CLI no longer needs a JavaScript runtime on your PATH to run plugins. A plugin that fails to load no longer silently loses its tools: Cline prints a warning naming the plugin and the error, `cline config tools --json` lists it as a `plugin_failure` entry, and the new `cline hub plugins` shows each plugin's status and last error (`--reload <plugin>` re-imports one without restarting the hub). Set `CLINE_PLUGIN_MODE=sandbox` to keep the old subprocess behavior
- `--thinking` now applies in ACP mode (`--acp`). Before, ACP sessions always ran with reasoning off
- `cline hook` accepts `agent_error` events. Before, it exited with an error and no response
- A provider API key set in the environment (such as `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`) now counts as configured at startup, for providers that read a single environment variable. Before, the TUI asked you to set up the provider anyway
- With no model chosen, the Cline provider now uses the first model in Cline's recommended list (Claude Sonnet 5.5)
- Turning reasoning off now works on every provider. Models that can't turn it off keep their default, and level-only Gemini models no longer reject the request with a thinking-budget error
- Screenshots and other images no longer inflate the token estimate, which made auto-compaction run long before the conversation was near its limit
- Auto-compaction uses the selected model's context window when the catalog entry has none
- Scheduled runs: queued runs now start instead of staying pending forever, a run whose model call fails (for example, a retired model) is marked failed with the error, and after downtime only the latest missed occurrence of a schedule runs instead of every one back to back
- Rule files that are symlinks now load
- Skills in `.claude/skills` are now discovered
- The editor tool no longer receives null in place of the text to replace from some models
- Refreshed the model catalog. Adds the AI/ML API, LowRouter, and Prime Inference providers. The v0 provider now offers only its default model, `v0-1.5-md`, and OpenCode Go uses its new `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1` endpoint. The Cline free list adds Step 5 Preview. Default models change for 302.AI, CrossModel, Cortecs, DigitalOcean, NEAR AI Cloud, and Ofox (Claude Haiku 5.5), DevPass (LLM Gateway), LLM Gateway, and Meta (Muse Wonder 1.0), Aixy (GPT-6.1 Sol), CloudFerro Sherlock and Moark (GLM 5.3), Ambient, NanoGPT, Neuralwatt, and Novita AI

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/cline/cline/compare/cli-v3.0.70...cli-v3.0.71

name: Supermemory Local 0.0.9
body:
- Added prebuilt Docker images for Linux amd64 and arm64.
- Improved Local uploads, namespace operations, search scoping and CLI commands.
- Added API v5 support. See the [API v5 upgrade guide](https://supermemory.ai/changelog/supermemory-api-v5/).

Before upgrading, back up your store and keep your existing directory and API key. Localhost requests now require the key; `WORKFLOW_ENGINE=direct` is no longer supported.

Before migrating an existing store, Local verifies a complete original backup. Existing cleanup can remove older duplicate documents and their source links.

Native Windows remains on 0.0.8 for now.

body:
> AI API Gateway Platform - 将 AI 订阅配额分发和管理

- Gemini 显式上下文缓存：支持创建、续期、删除缓存，内置官方存储价并按 Pro / Flash 系列兜底，存储费按 API Key 额度与订阅额度预留校验
- Gemini Vertex（Agent Platform）：支持 API Key 认证，服务账号支持同步上游模型列表，模型列表与详情接口支持 Vertex 账号
- Gemini AI Studio：适配新的 AQ. 格式 Key
- 临时不可调度规则新增作用范围选项：可选择命中后暂停整个账号或只冷却当前模型，未设置的存量规则行为不变
- 分组名称与描述支持多语言
- 运维请求详情表新增账号名称列

## 优化改进

- 第三方上游 API Key 与 Vertex 账号不再套用 AI Studio 等级和模拟配额

- Kimi 国际版 Coding 端点（api.kimi.ai）支持配额查询

## Bug 修复

- 修复上游拒绝结构化输入时 Chat 回退重试的问题，并保留 Responses 语义、避免不安全重试
- 修复 Kimi / DeepSeek / MiniMax 等非 OpenAI 账号被注入 Codex 图像生成桥接导致 400 的问题
- 修复 Gemini 引用不存在的缓存返回 403 时账号被停用并换号的问题
- 修复 Gemini 工具结果中的图片丢失问题
- 修复 Antigravity 图像模型限流影响同账号其他模型的问题
- 修复显式模型级 401 规则在故障转移、计数、Bedrock 等入口未生效、仍整号置错的问题
- 修复 Gemini 原生路由网关本地错误在运维中的归类问题
- 修复 Gemini 授权链接生成失败时错误信息丢失的问题
- 修复同步上游模型失败时未显示后端错误原因的问题
- 修复风控审核范围中残留已删除分组的问题
- 修复分组 RPM 覆盖加载过期数据的问题，并拒绝非正数的倍率修改
- 修复支付二维码倒计时漂移、用量倒计时切回标签页不刷新的问题
- 修复渠道监控 v2 设置无法添加缺失平台、自动刷新不更新缓存可用性的问题
- 修复运维自定义时间范围未按本地时区初始化的问题
- 修复下拉选择框在输入法组字时键盘输入被打断的问题

name: v13.37.0
body:
This release fixes the broken 13.36.1 marketplace update. After that update, the worker, the MCP search server and the server runtime failed to start, so memory capture stopped. Upgrading is strongly recommended.

## Fixes

- **claude-mem starts again after the 13.36.1 marketplace update** (#4728, #4729). A change merged after the 13.36.1 release committed the built plugin files with leftover `git stash` conflict markers. The plugin installs from `main`, so auto-updated installs got those files under the same 13.36.1 version number. The worker failed with `error: Unexpected <<`, `mcp-search` closed its connection, and memory capture stopped once the older worker exited. The files are now rebuilt from clean source. The npm package `claude-mem@13.36.1` was published before that change and was not affected. Thank you @nashsibanda for the rebuild and @hirohisatanigawa for the detailed report.
- **Worker startup waits out a locked database instead of failing** (#4725). The schema-writer check added in 13.36.0 ran before the connection's busy timeout was set. A worker starting while another process was opening the same database failed in about 1 ms with `database is locked`, and after two failures it was not restarted. The check now waits for the lock.

## Changed

- **Memory keeps capturing on your Anthropic plan when your selected provider can't serve** (#4727). `CLAUDE_MEM_QUOTA_FALLBACK_PROVIDER` now defaults to `claude`. Settings files that saved `""` get the new default too. The fallback now also covers a provider that is still rate limited or over capacity after its retries, is down, or returns the same batch twice with no usable output. Claude is used only when a Claude Code login or an Anthropic key is available. Memory moves back to your provider once it answers again. To wait for your provider instead, set `CLAUDE_MEM_QUOTA_FALLBACK_PROVIDER` to `off`.

## Release safety

- CI now checks the committed plugin files before it rebuilds them. It fails on merge-conflict markers anywhere in `plugin/` and runs `node --check` on every committed plugin script (#4729). Before this, CI rebuilt the bundles first and tested the rebuilt copies, which hid the broken committed ones.

## If you used the 13.35.0 workaround

If you followed the workaround in #4728 (auto-update turned off and the plugin pinned to 13.35.0), turn `autoUpdate` back on for the `thedotmack` marketplace and restart Claude Code to move to 13.37.0.

**Full diff:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v13.36.1...v13.37.0

name: v13.36.1
body:
A patch release that closes three issues found in review of 13.36.0, plus eight community fixes. Upgrading is recommended.

## Privacy and data safety

- **`<private>` content no longer leaves the hook in server runtime** (#4721). In server runtime, file edits, tool inputs and outputs, and session-start prompts were sent to the server with `<private>` sections still inside, and the server kept them in the raw event record (they were removed only later, when the model prompt was built). Private sections are now removed before anything leaves the hook, and the server removes them again before it stores events or session metadata. Worker runtime (the default) was not affected.
- **Older and newer workers can no longer race on a database upgrade** (#4724). The check that stops an older claude-mem from opening a database a newer version upgraded now reads and records the schema writer inside one SQLite write lock, before any migration runs. Before, two workers opening the database at the same moment could both pass the check.
- **A cancelled Chroma connection can no longer release a newer connection's lock** (#4722). Each Chroma connection now owns its writer-lock token and releases only that lock, so a reconnect during shutdown can't leave the new sidecar unlocked and allow a second writer on the same store. Process-table parsing for the orphan sweep now has fixture tests.

## Community fixes — thank you @rudycelekli

- Integration ids such as `constructor` no longer resolve through the alias table (#4712)
- Postgres numeric settings accept only whole positive numbers; values like `5ms` fall back to the default (#4713)
- Gemini retry hints too large to represent are ignored, so a key isn't parked indefinitely (#4714)
- The billing-type file is read correctly when it starts with a UTF-8 BOM (#4715)
- API-key settings arrays keep only string entries (#4716)
- A malformed part in a Gemini response no longer discards the whole answer (#4717)
- Refused connections are recognized inside wrapped errors, so recovery kicks in (#4718)
- Hook launchers honor the environment opt-out flags before starting Node or Bun (#4719)

**Full diff:** https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/compare/v13.36.0...v13.36.1

name: v13.36.0
body:
A community release: nearly every change since v13.35.0 came from outside contributors and is merged under their own name. Thank you all.

## Highlights

- **Memories are no longer dropped when the provider says no.** An empty Anthropic credit balance, an organization blocking subscription access, or a local model server that is down now pauses the observer and keeps the work instead of discarding it (@Mola-maker). When the observer stream ends early, its batch is handed back for reprocessing (@shantanukhanwalkar).
- **Windows home folders with non-ASCII names work again.** Bun and Claude are found when your user folder name contains Korean, Japanese or other non-ASCII characters (@akushonkamen).
- **Hooks don't report your project's tsconfig as errors.** This affected React Native and Expo projects (@Totopo27).
- **The viewer saves only what you changed,** so an old settings tab can't undo a change you made elsewhere (@Cassian433).
- **Search improvements:**
  - Correct paging (@junnhwan).
  - Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Thai words are found inside sentences (@rudycelekli).
  - Long natural-language queries fall back to any-term matching when no memory matches every word (@devkancheti4-design).
- **Chroma reliability:**
  - No more stalls after a reboot on large stores (@akushonkamen).
  - Orphaned chroma-mcp processes that hold your data directory are cleaned up safely before starting, so they no longer cause lock fights (@akushonkamen).

## New

- **Qoder** plugin support (@shouldnotappearcalm).
- **Screenpipe** skill for searching meeting and screen history and saving it to memory (@EzraEllette).
- **Atlas Cloud** preset for the OpenAI-compatible provider (@binyangzhu000-sudo).
- **`CLAUDE_MEM_OPENROUTER_TEMPERATURE`** setting (@aeneasr).
- **`CLAUDE_MEM_SEMANTIC_INJECT_FORMAT=index`:** compact per-prompt memory injection (@ktdrv).
- **`CLAUDE_MEM_WORK_STATE_ENABLED=false`** to turn off the work-state to-do rule (@noesis-bot).
- **`CLAUDE_MEM_TOOL_USES_RETENTION_DAYS`:** opt-in pruning of the raw tool log. The default keeps everything (@Montinou).
- **Duplicate review:** record a "distinct" or "dismissed" verdict on duplicate candidates (@Montinou).
- **Viewer:** a Claude auth method control in settings (@akushonkamen).
- **Server runtime:** idempotent memory uploads (@escooterclinic).

## Fixes

- **Capture and sessions:**
  - Original capture timestamps are kept for delayed events (@junnhwan).
  - Stale session-end events are retired (@akushonkamen).
  - Warnings are logged before queued work is discarded (@Boulea7).
  - Tool calls whose input is `null` are captured, logging recovers when the log folder appears later, and every shutdown step runs (@rudycelekli).
  - Search triggers are restored after database upgrades (@akushonkamen).
  - Fewer SQLite warnings on macOS (@CCCLL).
- **Database safety:** the database records the newest schema version that has written to it, and an older claude-mem refuses to open a database a newer one has upgraded (@akushonkamen).
- **Memory import and notes:**
  - Restored memories attach to existing sessions (@junnhwan).
  - Native note revisions survive title dedup (@junnhwan).
  - Explicit notes keep their platform source in the search index (@junnhwan).
  - Notes that start with `----` are no longer mangled (@akushonkamen).
- **Search robustness:** malformed file lists, plain-text concepts, folder search against absolute paths, consistent date parsing, and better patterns for native search commands (@rudycelekli).
- **Installers and integrations:**
  - Cursor configs with a BOM and commented Codex TOML are read correctly, and npm can no longer hang the installer (@rudycelekli).
  - Worker ports and IPv6 addresses are honored everywhere, and the uvx path can be set in settings (@Ravencloned).
- **Providers and streaming:**
  - OpenCode Go session header (@Cassian433).
  - Sturdier streamed replies, emoji never split when long output is trimmed, and Zstandard transcripts keep their text intact (@rudycelekli).
- **Server runtime:**
  - Fresh installs no longer get 403 errors (@DeryFerd).
  - File edits reach the server, and `CLAUDE_MEM_SKIP_TOOLS` is honored in server mode (@DeryFerd).
  - Stuck jobs are reclaimed (@escooterclinic).
  - No stray local database (@vinay121314).
  - Leaner prompts (@rich-murphey).
  - Postgres keeps literal `__proto__` keys in stored JSON (@rudycelekli).
  - Stricter Redis settings (@rudycelekli).
- **Sync, Chroma and duplicates:**
  - Prompts from other devices are linked (@necatisozer).
  - Turning Chroma off is fully honored (@CCCLL).
  - Fewer Chroma rewrites at startup (@Montinou).
  - Accent-aware duplicate detection (@rudycelekli) and a corrected similarity threshold (@udsy19).
- **Viewer:**
  - "Select all" in the Logs drawer works (@DrDLyuan).
  - The context preview opens on a project that has data (@rudycelekli).

## Project

- `main` is now the only branch. `core-dev` and `community-edge` are retired, so please open pull requests against `main`.

# OpenWhispr 1.10.3

The assistant can now act in other apps: it drafts and sends email, posts to Slack, and works with Linear and GitHub issues, always behind a card you approve. Notes get templates for the AI Summary, actions that answer in a docked chat, and real tables. OpenWhispr also uses far less memory when idle, shows a plain-language error when your API key or provider fails, and fixes a long list of bugs on Linux, Windows and macOS.

## 🌟 Highlights

- **🔌 Connectors** — The assistant can draft and send email (Gmail), post to Slack, and work with Linear and GitHub issues. Nothing goes out until you press **Send** on a card showing exactly what will be sent. Paid plans; connect in Settings → Integrations. (#2331, #2369, #2385, #2401, #2402)
- **📝 Note templates and actions** — Templates shape the AI Summary, and actions like Follow-up email answer in a chat docked beside the note instead of overwriting your summary. (#2397, #2557, #2578, #2598)
- **📊 Tables in notes** — Tables stay tables when you edit a note, and a formatting toolbar appears when you select text. (#2255)
- **🪶 Lighter when idle** — Search and meeting detection only run when needed, cutting idle memory use from about 500 MB. (#2299, #2371)
- **💬 Clear error messages** — When your own API key or provider fails, you get a plain-language message with a link to fix it. (#2510)

## ✨ Also new

Echo cancellation for meetings, an option to keep the local model loaded, a folder picker in the meeting notification, dictation audio that survives a crash, a macOS permission helper in onboarding, Apple sign-in on Windows and Linux, and live speaker names on Linux.

## 🛠 Fixes

- **Windows:** Teams meetings record everyone for the whole call again. (#2233)
- **Transcription:** API key changes apply without a restart, and AssemblyAI, Corti and Gemini Live no longer drop words.
- **Assistant:** Answers paste as plain text, follow-ups don't repeat actions already sent, and images in replies are no longer loaded automatically.
- **Linux:** GPU rendering is back (except on NVIDIA), Settings no longer lags, and paste waits for you to release held keys.
- **Notes and meetings:** Assistant edits to a note can be undone and never wipe fields by accident, clearing a note now syncs, and fixes for Join & transcribe, live transcripts on reload, and TXT export. (#2602, #2604)

## ⚠️ Heads-up

The Windows portable `.exe` is discontinued. Use the installer instead. (#2301)

The full list is in the [changelog](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#1103---2026-10-12).

## 🙏 Thanks

Thanks to @Chadpiha, @boseq, @greatcoat, @hsusul, @IdrisGit, @clarkmaan, @Nathan-Roll1, @gabrielste1n, @sochotnicky, @kuleje, @TrackerGit, @zhongwater123, @emanuelet, @marselsel, @folks-samuel-cb, @STiFLeR7, @Adityakk9031, @stantheman0128, @cadufpolis, @Abhishek-B-R, @dajiaohuang and @hiro-nikaitou for their work on this release. 🎉

And thanks to @jaszczurovsky, @TaiFeng, @jsholcomb, @wadamek65, @KishenG and @amarpreet2209 for reporting and narrowing down the Teams capture bug (#1265).

## 0.9.89 (2026-10-13)

Sixteen community pull requests: cross-repo member-call resolution (Go, PHP, TypeScript, Kotlin, Objective-C), generic/template type-parameter cleanup (Kotlin, Scala, C++, Swift), an Objective-C enum extractor, interface-dispatch fan-out, a native Pi guard extension, and several resolution/ingest fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

- Feature: **cross-repo member calls** now finish across a repository boundary for Go, PHP, TypeScript/JS, Kotlin and Objective-C: a call whose receiver type is declared in another repo is parked by name during the single-repo build and bound on `merge-graphs`/`global add` against a unique same-named exported type, fail-closed on ambiguity (#3152, #3388, #3393, #3385, #3387, #3389, #3391, #3395, thanks @xiongjianxu).
- Fix: **Go** a package's type whose methods span several files now folds into one node instead of fragmenting under `_disambiguate_colliding_node_ids`, so single-definition guards and receiver typing work (#3399, #3400, thanks @xiongjianxu).
- Fix: **Kotlin / Scala / C++ / Swift** generic and template type parameters (`class Box<T>`, `[T]`, `template<typename T>`, `struct Stack<Element>`) no longer mint sourceless stub god-nodes; a real same-named type is still referenced (#4406, #4407, #4408, #4409, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Feature: **Objective-C** `NS_ENUM` and `NS_OPTIONS` declarations are now extracted as an enum type plus its members, with the macro forms validated and malformed macros rejected fail-closed (#4400, #4401, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).
- Feature: **dispatch** an interface member now links to every implementer, not just one, so a DI chain through a multi-implementer interface resolves; the fan-out is gated to genuine implementers with a correct method match (#3800, #4396, thanks @Goodkamalpandey).
- Feature: **Pi** a native Pi guard extension now runs `graphify hook-guard` before Pi's tool calls and also loads under Oh My Pi, so the hook-guard policy reaches Pi; install/uninstall delegates to `pi install`/`pi remove` and the guard fails open (#4378, thanks @andrebrait).
- Feature: **hook** a firing read/search nudge now shows the graph nodes behind the nudged call and tightens its wording, so agents act on it instead of treating it as noise; the graph read piggybacks on the already-bounded nudge and is injection-safe and size-capped (#4368, thanks @andrebrait).
- Fix: **resolution** a `.js` import now resolves to a `.tsx` source when no real `.js` file exists, matching TypeScript's NodeNext resolution; a real `.js` still wins (#3486, #4395, thanks @DevChiniwala).
- Fix: distinct downloaded binary captures (PDFs/images) whose URLs collide to one filename are now kept under numbered names instead of silently overwriting each other, matching the markdown path's de-dup (#4393, #4394, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

name: v0.9.88
body:
## 0.9.88 (2026-10-12)

Twenty community pull requests: language-extraction and call-resolution fixes (Java, C/C++, Python, Swift, Go, PowerShell, C#, JS/EJS), dedup/shrink-guard hardening, and query/graph.html ergonomics. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

- Feature: **Java** a call on a chained, `new` or cast receiver (`factory.builder().size(3).build()`, `new Builder().size(1)`, `((Builder) o).build()`) now resolves through the declared return types on the method chain, binding only on a single unambiguous target (#4306, #4307, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **Java** a bare call or field receiver inherited from a supertype in another file now resolves to the nearest declaring supertype (class wins over an interface default; a tie binds nothing), instead of dangling (#4304, #4305, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **C/C++** a quoted cross-directory include (`#include "../lib/foo.h"`, STM32 `Core/Src` to `Core/Inc`) now resolves to the right header by a unique longest-shared-directory-prefix match, fail-closed on ties and never guessing for `./`, `../`, absolute or angle-bracket includes (#4354, #4392, thanks @hopstreax).
- Fix: **Python** a `@name.setter`/`.getter`/`.deleter` decorator no longer mints a sourceless stub node (#4380, #4385, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Fix: **Python** a `Self` (PEP 673) type annotation (`-> Self`, `: Self`, `typing.Self`) no longer mints a sourceless `self` stub (#4381, #4386, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Fix: **Swift** a `Self` type annotation no longer mints a sourceless `self` stub (#4382, #4387, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Fix: **Go** generic type parameters (`[T any]`) in signatures, struct fields and interface methods no longer mint sourceless `t`/`r` stubs (#4383, #4388, thanks @rajatnagda45).
- Fix: **Python** a class type-hinted before it is defined (a forward reference) no longer mints a bare stub that collides with and swallows the file node (#4334, #4343, thanks @Mpasha17).
- Fix: **C#** extraction now recovers members declared after a verbatim interpolated string that ends in an escaped quote (`$@"a""{e}"""`), instead of silently dropping the rest of the file; the fix masks only the offending bytes and discards the rewrite unless it re-parses clean (#3376, #3612, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Fix: **PowerShell** dot-sourced includes with quoted or `$PSScriptRoot` paths now emit import edges, and script-scope commands (outside any function) are now collected as calls (#4356, #4369, thanks @FabioRueda).
- Fix: **JS/TS** a bare or scoped external import is now anchored to the package name rather than the path leaf, so `@scope-a/utils` and `@scope-b/utils` stay distinct and `lodash/fp/map` collapses onto one `lodash` node (#3084, #3092, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Feature: **EJS** (`.ejs`) templates now have an extractor: scriptlet functions/classes, require/import edges, dynamic imports, and `<%- include('partial') %>` composition edges, instead of a single top-level parse error (#3811, #4338, thanks @nothariharan).
- Fix: **serve** a dotted Python query (`pkg.mod.func`, `pkg.mod:func`) now resolves to the symbol by module path, fail-closed on a same-file ambiguity, without regressing bare-name lookups (#4366, #4367, thanks @Mpasha17).
- Fix: dedup now path-qualifies semantic ids that dropped the directory, so `a/x.md` and `b/x.md` (both minting a bare `x`) stay distinct instead of collapsing and losing one node; a reference to the bare id from a third file is left unresolved with a warning rather than guessed (#4281, #4362, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).
- Fix: a semantic node that dedup legitimately folded into its AST twin is now exempt from the shrink guard, so `graphify update` on a graph that had an LLM semantic ghost is no longer wrongly write-blocked; the exemption is scoped to a strict `_origin=="ast"` twin at the same path and label, so a genuine partial-build loss is still refused. LLM node/edge field aliases (`file`/`filepath`, `relationship`) are folded, with the canonical field always winning (#4389, #4391, thanks @AndresDiagoM).
- Fix: **install** `graphify install/uninstall` now removes only graphify's own hook entries (keyed on the `hook-guard`/`hook-check` command, not a loose "graphify" substring), keeping co-located user hooks and other commands in the same group, and routes uninstall through a backup (#4359, #4373, thanks @nothariharan).
- Fix: **install** CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and sibling files now keep their original line endings (CRLF or LF) across install and uninstall, instead of being normalized to the platform default (#4360, #4372, thanks @nothariharan).
- Fix: **wiki** index rows now link to their own article when two communities or god-nodes share a label, instead of both pointing at the first-registered slug and orphaning the second article (#3032, #3033, #3095, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).
- Feature: **query** `--seed` starts the traversal at given nodes (ids, labels, callable names or paths) so an external ranker can choose the start set; unresolved seeds are reported and skipped, and an all-unresolved set fails closed rather than falling back to keyword seeds (#4293, #4289, thanks @devkancheti4-design).
- Feature: **graph.html** the sidebar now shows a hover tooltip with the full (truncated) legend/search/neighbor name and the legend node count; user text is written via `textContent`, preserving the embedded-JSON escaping (#4286, #4291, thanks @Hassannzidan).

name: v2026.1012.0
body:
# Paperclip v2026.1012.0

> Released: 2026-10-12

Paperclip v2026.1012.0 carries 130 commits, promoted from `2026.1006.0-beta.0`. The headline is that outside assistants can now join your team: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and any MCP client can connect to Paperclip as a signed-in person, review work, and delegate tasks, all behind an experimental setting. Around that: Chat leads the navigation with each agent's tasks and artifacts beside the conversation, the Connections catalog pulls in accounts you already linked in Composio and Arcade, connections carry usage instructions that reach your agents automatically, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol arrive with refreshed harnesses, and agents can safely update company skills. Underneath, Codex runs survive server restarts and model-capacity errors, workspace restore locks move to crash-safe SQLite file locks, and default agent instructions shrink to a fraction of their former size.

## Breaking Changes

- **Workspace restore locks change protocol; stop every old process before upgrading.** Restore and agent-file collection locks are now OS-backed SQLite file locks under `<instance root>/locks/directory-merge/`, released by the kernel when a process crashes. Old and new versions must not write to the same instance root at once: drain and stop all old server and worker processes (including other hosts or containers) before upgrading or rolling back, then move any leftover legacy `<hash>.lock/` directories to a scratch location. Never delete or move the new `.lock.sqlite` files. See `doc/workspace-restore-locks.md`. ([#14869](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14869))
- **Stored tool grants are enforced as written.** A grant whose `scope.allow` list does not match a tool, connection, or application no longer falls through to a broader policy; grants with unknown selectors or malformed restrictions now deny access. Review custom grants after upgrading if an agent loses a tool it previously used. ([#14915](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14915))

## Highlights

- **Assistants join your team over MCP** — A new "Assistant Connection (MCP)" card in Connections lets Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and generic MCP clients connect to Paperclip through browser OAuth or device-code consent and act as the signed-in user: read and search tasks, create and delegate work, leave human comments, read documents and deliverables, and follow results through signed event webhooks ([#14846](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14846)). Consent shows the client and organization, write access can be opted out, requests can be pinned to one company, and a `paperclip mcp` CLI device login bridges local stdio clients; it is off by default behind Settings → Experimental → "Assistant connections (MCP)" and requires an HTTPS `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` ([#14933](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14933)).
- **Chat leads the way** — With Agent Chat enabled in the streamlined UI (the default shell), Chat is the first row in the Work navigation, the chat rail lists every eligible agent, and the side panel shows that agent's recent tasks and artifacts; a new experimental "Combined Inbox + Task List" setting folds Inbox into Tasks as views ([#15100](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15100)). Instances that switched "Streamlined UI" off keep the legacy navigation and do not see these changes. The Chat entry reopens the last conversation you visited ([#14848](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14848)), and the chat header shows the agent's avatar ([#14726](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14726)).
- **One catalog for every account** — The Connections Apps catalog discovers accounts already connected upstream in Composio, Arcade, and supported Executor gateways and groups them with native accounts under one app card, with source chips, search, and pagination ([#15254](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15254)). AgentMail is a default connection with inline setup cards in Agent Chat ([#14772](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14772)), Neon joins the catalog with OAuth or API-key sign-in ([#14980](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14980)), Asana works again with a default "Sign in with Asana" ([#14756](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14756)), and AI accounts gain a "Check usage" action that reads current provider limits for Codex, Claude, Grok, and OpenRouter ([#14936](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14936)).
- **Connections carry instructions for agents** — A connection can hold editable usage instructions that are delivered to every authorized agent turn across the native runner, legacy adapters, and HTTP/process contracts. Honcho, Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, and Cognee ship defaults, the editor appears in setup and the Permissions panel, and agent Instructions show a read-only "From connections" section ([#15216](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15216)).
- **New models, refreshed harnesses** — Claude Sonnet 5.5 is selectable for Claude Code agents with Low through Max effort, and the qualified Claude runtime moves to Claude Code 2.1.286 ([#14993](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14993)); GPT-6.1 Sol joins the Codex adapter with Fast mode and Ultra effort, Bedrock gains Sonnet 5.5, and the shared pins move to Codex 0.160.0 and OpenCode 1.18.34 ([#14942](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14942)). Claude and Codex model menus now list models in the same order as the Claude and ChatGPT apps ([#14917](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14917), [#14918](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14918)).
- **Agents maintain company skills** — Native-runner agents get an `update_skill` tool that rewrites a company skill with version checking and safe retries, recorded in version history and the audit log; the skill file API gains optional `expectedVersionId` and `idempotencyKey` fields ([#15049](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15049)). Newly created agents receive a default set of configuration grants so they can finish agent, tool, skill, and task setup without manual permission work ([#15283](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15283)).
- **Codex runs that survive restarts and capacity limits** — A native Codex turn killed by a server restart resumes in the same conversation once the old process is proven gone ([#15297](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15297)); a model at capacity shows a "Model at capacity" card and retries automatically after one and then two minutes ([#15347](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15347)); a model the ChatGPT account cannot use shows "Model unavailable" with guidance instead of generic recovery ([#15299](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15299), [#15304](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15304)); and Codex keeps its stock base prompt, receiving Paperclip's context as additive developer instructions ([#14920](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14920)).
- **A rebuilt New task dialog** — The dialog is built on the shared task composer with a Project and Worktrees bar, remembered assignee, project, and effort, and task mentions in suggestions; the status, reviewer, approver, and watchdog controls move out of the dialog into task properties, and new tasks default to the last assignee used ([#15091](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15091)). Tasks created without a title get a clean plain-text provisional title ([#15047](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15047)).
- **Far shorter default instructions** — New companies and hires get role descriptions instead of procedural manuals: the default CEO instructions drop from roughly 1,900 words to 20 ([#14985](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14985)), new non-CEO hires receive a one-sentence default manual ([#14948](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14948)), and the bundled planning skills shrink to about 400 words combined and no longer force a child-task matrix ([#15296](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15296)). Existing saved manuals and custom bundles are unchanged.

## Fixes

- **Native runner and sessions** — A run whose final answer was saved but whose shutdown failed reaches its correct final status, and the agent `list_projects` tool returns paged summaries instead of overflowing the command limit ([#15217](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15217)); tasks stopped during native preparation on an older build regain Retry and accept new messages ([#15020](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15020), [#15022](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15022)); a continuation cancelled by the queued-run review gate is treated as a review wait instead of an unknown-execution hold ([#15024](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15024)); Retry and saved-message recovery work on `SQL_ASCII` databases ([#15033](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15033)); a user-continued legacy run that times out can be retried automatically ([#14987](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14987)); a completed run no longer reports "Run failed" when instruction-file cleanup times out afterward ([#14945](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14945)) and that cleanup no longer blocks lease release ([#14866](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14866)); `write_document` and other semantic tool calls no longer fail when a document merely discusses credentials ([#14937](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14937)) or contains credential-looking text ([#15301](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15301)); long connected MCP tool names are aliased to fit provider limits and the recovery notice explains why a run was cancelled with a Continue option ([#14951](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14951)); agents keep their task context when a tool connection changes mid-task ([#14963](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14963)); native MCP gateways reject run tokens from any agent other than their owner ([#14914](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14914)); and the Codex runner's "ignored unrelated provider information" warnings stay in the run log instead of the chat ([#14929](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14929)).
- **Sandboxes and workspaces** — Sandbox runs no longer fail with `workspace_restore_failed` after an agent rebases or amends its branch ([#15268](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15268)); the Daytona driver recovers output from a log socket that goes silent ([#14889](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14889)); bridge control commands are capped at 30 seconds and active runs are flagged as suspicious after 5 minutes of silence and critical after 15 ([#14979](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14979)); multi-repository projects round-trip commits on SSH execution environments ([#14782](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14782)); isolated-worktree tasks on the Paperclip repository itself set up without a local seed config ([#14810](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14810)); and the standard Docker image bundles the remote provider pack so remote OpenCode and ACPX runs no longer fail with `runner_remote_provider_artifact_incompatible` ([#14854](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14854)).
- **Chat and task UI** — Steer and Interrupt show your message immediately and deliver to the active run even after a model or effort change, and a stopped native startup offers Retry ([#15015](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15015)); a message sent after a failed native run no longer hangs and is delivered exactly once ([#14857](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14857)); stale "Run failed", "Stopped", and "Waiting to resume" markers disappear once a later attempt supersedes them ([#14874](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14874)); dismissed agent questions stay in the task feed and remain answerable ([#15229](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15229)); confirmation cards show "Preparing approval…" until the source workspace is ready instead of erroring on click ([#14893](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14893)); an unsaved Agent Chat no longer polls the browser panel with a draft id every three seconds ([#15298](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15298)); the thread no longer calls a stale send or cancel action ([#14863](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14863)); mobile task pages get an opaque footer, steadier scrolling, a full-height document panel, and in-place document links ([#15228](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15228)) with new output staying above the composer ([#15282](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15282)); the completed-work caret sits beside its label ([#15048](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15048)), composer labels use the available width ([#15050](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15050)), branch artifacts without a remote link say so ([#15051](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15051)), the Dashboard shows each task once ([#14847](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14847)), and a selected saved subscription can be used without clicking the provider tile ([#14996](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14996)).
- **Connections and access** — Agent settings can reconnect an unavailable personal AI account in place, and a newly connected account becomes the user's default ([#14916](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14916)); generic MCP OAuth requests `offline_access` when offered so access survives token expiry ([#14950](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14950)); MCP tool discovery uses a fraction of the memory and queries on large catalogs, bounds concurrent listings with a `tool_discovery_busy` 503 under load, and answers GET on stateless endpoints with 405 ([#14864](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14864)); low-trust agents can create self-assigned work inside their permitted scope and update their own managed `AGENTS.md` from the owner's chat ([#14870](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14870)) and accept their owner's direct messages and human-assigned tasks outside an intake boundary ([#14775](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14775)); company skill imports from a server-managed project checkout no longer fail with `skill_workspace_boundary_denied` ([#10329](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/10329)); and the managed `git`/`gh` launcher retries a failed credential broker request before continuing without managed credentials ([#14856](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14856)).
- **Server resilience** — Dashboard reads ([#14873](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14873)), scoped read queries ([#15248](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15248)), and the task run list ([#15300](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15300)) retry transient PostgreSQL disconnects instead of failing the request, and routine routes return 404 for malformed ids instead of a database error ([#15313](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15313)).

## Improvements

- Experimental AI connection pools rotate new tasks across saved AI accounts while each task stays pinned to its account, behind the default-off `enableAiConnectionRouters` setting and a router plugin ([#14967](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14967)); the exe.dev sandbox provider can clone a prepared "Source VM" instead of creating a bare one ([#14975](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14975)); the native runner daemon accepts any `--listen-port` so several listening runners can share a host ([#15353](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15353)); the server keeps a durable lifecycle journal of agent hire, pause, resume, and terminate events and project create and update events as groundwork for plugin hooks ([#15280](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15280), [#15306](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15306)); Slack, GitHub, MCP, invitation, routine, and handoff prompts share one animated "copy prompt" control ([#14862](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14862)) and the Slack setup prompt matches the current flow ([#14965](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14965)); the per-action Test dialog renders MCP results as readable tables and cards ([#14859](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14859)); agents can create question cards from a single canonical question set ([#14946](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14946)) and receive identical completion-tool guidance across Codex, Claude, and OpenCode ([#14961](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14961)) with less repeated procedure text and a canonical link from `write_document` ([#15151](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15151)); and failed restores and Stop timeouts record which stage failed and why in run results and Sentry context ([#15005](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15005), [#15291](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15291), [#14990](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14990), [#14986](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14986)).

## Upgrade Guide

- **Migrations `0294`–`0305`** run on upgrade: `0294` adds a `tool_mcp_gateway_tokens` expiry index; `0295` and `0296` add aggregator account snapshot and sync tables; `0297` adds `resource_lifecycle_events` and `0300` rewrites its action check constraint; `0298` adds `tool_connections.agent_instructions` and backfills default instructions for existing Honcho, Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, and Cognee connections; `0299` adds AI connection pool, router cursor, and task pin tables plus `company_secrets.ai_session_epoch`; `0301`–`0305` add the public MCP OAuth client, grant, token, receipt, event subscription, device-flow, and admission tables. All are additive; `0298` is the only one that updates existing rows.
- **Stop all old processes before upgrading** ([#14869](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14869)): the new SQLite restore-lock protocol cannot coexist with the old directory locks. Drain every server and worker that writes to the instance root, move leftover legacy `<hash>.lock/` directories out of `<instance root>/locks/directory-merge/`, then start the new version. The same applies to rollback.
- **Review custom tool grants** ([#14915](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14915)): grants with unknown scope selectors or malformed restrictions now deny instead of falling through.
- **New experimental settings**, all off by default: "Assistant connections (MCP)" (`enablePublicMcp`) exposes the public MCP endpoint and requires `PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL` to be an HTTPS origin ([#14933](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14933)); "Combined Inbox + Task List" (`enableCombinedInboxTasks`) folds Inbox into Tasks and takes effect only while "Streamlined UI" is on ([#15100](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15100)); `enableAiConnectionRouters` turns on connection pools and has no UI toggle ([#14967](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14967)).
- **Connection instructions for custom adapters** ([#15216](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15216)): HTTP adapters receive a top-level `connectionInstructions` field in the request body, either a `{ text, digest }` object or `null` when no instructions apply; process adapters receive `PAPERCLIP_CONNECTION_INSTRUCTIONS_FILE`, the path to a private JSON file holding the same `{ text, digest }` object, and the variable is set to an empty string (not a path) when no instructions apply. Adapters should append the object's `text` to the model prompt rather than passing the object through. Built-in harnesses need no change.
- **Harness pins moved** to Codex 0.160.0, Claude Agent SDK 0.3.286 (Claude Code 2.1.286), and OpenCode 1.18.34 ([#14942](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14942), [#14993](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14993)). Custom sandbox images built with Claude Code older than 2.1.284 must be rebuilt before Sonnet 5.5 works on the CLI path, and the controller and runner should be deployed before promoting a sandbox image with the new pins; remote Codex now accepts 0.149.0 up to but excluding 0.161.0.
- **New defaults**: newly created standard agents receive default configuration grants, while existing agents are unchanged ([#15283](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15283)); the runner's `--listen-port` still defaults to 43127 ([#15353](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/15353)); silent active runs are flagged after 5 and 15 minutes instead of 1 and 4 hours, with no automatic cancellation ([#14979](https://github.com/paperclipai/paperclip/pull/14979)).
- No other configuration or API changes require action.

# Cua Driver 0.35.2

## Summary

## Fixes

- name the missing AT-SPI bus in the X11 background keyboard refusal. ([#5070](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5070))
- scroll an inner Electron scroller in the background on macOS. ([#5079](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5079))
- tolerate a transient UIA read and a twice-reported consent prompt on Windows. ([#5082](https://github.com/trycua/cua/pull/5082))

## Contributors

This release contains maintainer changes only.

## Install

macOS and Linux:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://cua.ai/driver/install.sh)"
```

Windows:

```powershell
irm https://cua.ai/driver/install.ps1 | iex
```

Cua Driver ships universal macOS binaries, x86_64 and arm64 Windows builds,
and Linux preview builds. Release assets also include tag-pinned installer and
uninstaller scripts.

## Why GitHub says “Pre-release”

GitHub's label is used only to keep this monorepo's repository-wide “Latest”
pointer from switching between independently released products. A plain Cua
Driver SemVer is a stable release; npm and PyPI publish it on
their normal stable channels, and the installers resolve the versioned
`cua-driver-rs-v*` releases directly.

name: Orca Mobile Android mobile-android-v0.0.55
body:
Thank you for using Orca mobile! ❤️

## Over-the-air updates

The Orca app on your phone now gets most of its screens and features from the desktop it's paired with, instead of having them built into the app. When you update Orca on your computer, the phone picks up the new version the next time it connects.

- **New features sooner.** Phone improvements ship with each desktop release. You don't have to wait for an App Store or Play Store update.
- **Phone and desktop always match.** The phone runs the version your desktop serves, so features and fixes line up and nothing breaks because one side is newer.
- **Fewer app updates.** You only need to update the app itself occasionally.

You'll see a short "Downloading the latest app" screen the first time you connect to a computer, and again after you update Orca there. After that, the app opens right away.

## What's new

- When the app downloads the latest version from your computer, a progress bar shows how far along it is, and downloads finish faster.
- Grok, OpenCode, OMP and Pi chats now open on the phone, and chat visuals and subagents show inline like on desktop.
- Messages you send while an agent is working wait above the composer and go out in order. A message that couldn't be delivered is marked "Not sent" and goes back to your draft.
- Answer an agent's questions with number keys.
- SSH hosts show their connection health on the workspace list, and the list follows the desktop's pinned-workspace setting.
- Videos and music files play in file previews.
- Pairing links are more secure, and scanning a new code replaces an old pairing.
- Lower memory use, smoother chat scrolling on Android, and more reliable terminals.

Most phone features come from your desktop, so update Orca on your computer to get everything. See the [desktop release notes](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases) for the full list.
